title: Degree-zero Frobenius exchange is the underived section-pullback mate
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ with $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $a:Y\to s$. Write $g=g_Y$ and $h=g_s$ for the geometric Galois Frobenii, so $ag=ha$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the inverse image and module adjunctions [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and the finite derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Let $M$ be a constructible sheaf of $A_Y$-modules, placed in degree zero [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and assume $Ra_*M\in D^b_c(s,A)$, so that the point transport on it is in its stated domain. Use ordinary cohomology and the point fiber of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology, def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. For $u=g,h$, write $j^u_N:u^{-1}N\to u^*N$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, for the specified comparison [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](a), and $\lambda^u_N:u^*N\to u^{-1}N$ for its multiplication inverse, $x\otimes b\mapsto c_A^{u,-1}(b)x$ [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback].

Let $e_M=\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M):Lh^*Ra_*M\to Ra_*Lg^*M$ be the specified mate [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange](1). Let $B_M:h^{-1}a_*M\to a_*g^{-1}M$ be the UNDERIVED inverse-image mate: its transpose under $a^{-1}\dashv a_*$ is the square identification $a^{-1}h^{-1}a_*M\cong g^{-1}a^{-1}a_*M$ followed by $g^{-1}(\varepsilon^0_{a,M})$. Define $\sigma_{a_*M}:\Gamma(s,a_*M)\to\Gamma(s,h^{-1}a_*M)$ by restriction along $h:(s\xrightarrow{h}s)\to(s\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}s)$, insertion at $(s\xrightarrow{h}s)$ into the inverse-image colimit, and sheafification, exactly as in [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. Define $p_{g,M}:\Gamma(Y,M)\to\Gamma(Y,g^{-1}M)$ in the same way, using restriction along $g:(Y\xrightarrow{g}Y)\to(Y\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}Y)$ and insertion at $(Y\xrightarrow{g}Y)$. These definitions use the final objects of the sites, not a $k$-linear structure on $g$.

Using the canonical right-derived-zero identification $\mathcal H^0(Ra_*M)=a_*M$, exact finite pullback and exact sections on $s$ [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], the actual maps satisfy
$$a_*(\lambda^g_M)\circ\mathcal H^0(e_M)\circ(\lambda^h_{a_*M})^{-1}=B_M,$$
$$\mathrm H^0(\iota_{Ra_*M})=\Gamma(s,j^h_{a_*M})\circ\sigma_{a_*M},\qquad \Gamma(s,B_M)\circ\sigma_{a_*M}=p_{g,M}.$$
Here $\iota$ is the specified point transport, with the preceding canonical identifications of its source and target. In particular the ordinary transport $\tau_M=\operatorname{Fib}_s(e_M)\circ\iota_{Ra_*M}$ [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] satisfies
$$\Gamma(Y,\lambda^g_M)\circ\mathrm H^0(\tau_M)=p_{g,M}.$$
No properness, connectedness, Weil structure, or chosen unit section is assumed.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change (derived unit-square-counit mate); the degree-zero pro-etale Galois-Frobenius specialization and the explicit point-transport formula are stated by an agent for blueprint prop-cohomological-finiteness, Proof Step 7.

proof.text: By the Frobenius-square lemma, $g$ and $h$ are scheme isomorphisms, $ag=ha$, and the square is Cartesian. For a pro-etale test object $u:U\to s$, the Cartesian identification is $d_U:Y\times_{s,a,u}U\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\times_{s,a,hu}U$, $(y,v)\mapsto(g(y),v)$. Inverse image along an isomorphism is exact site relabelling, and finite-coefficient module pullback is this relabelling with the constant coefficient action transported. Thus the comparison $j^u_N$ is termwise $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, its inverse is the displayed $\lambda^u_N$, and all source and target identifications in the first equality are canonical.

source.place: Step 2; explicit power-square and site relabelling calculation

proof.text: Choose a K-injective complex $I$ representing $M$. The exact inverse images along the scheme isomorphisms preserve the relevant complexes, and a right adjoint of an exact functor preserves K-injectives, so $a_*I$ and the pulled-back complexes represent the derived operations. The exchange in [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] is the derived adjunction mate; the fraction characterization of the pre-derived adjunction identifies its degree-zero map with the underived chain map whose transpose is $a^{-1}h^{-1}a_*I\to g^{-1}a^{-1}a_*I\to g^{-1}I$. Applying the canonical right-derived-zero identification $\mathcal H^0(Ra_*M)=a_*M$ and the inverse comparisons $\lambda^h,\lambda^g$ gives $a_*(\lambda^g_M)\circ\mathcal H^0(e_M)\circ(\lambda^h_{a_*M})^{-1}=B_M$. Exactness of $\Gamma(s,-)$ identifies this sheaf-level calculation with the corresponding degree-zero calculation on sections.

source.place: Step 2; finite-level K-injective and derived-mate calculation

proof.text: For $N=Ra_*M$, the point transport is, by its definition, $\iota_N=\Gamma(s,j^h_{a_*M})\circ\sigma_{a_*M}$ after the canonical degree-zero identification. Since sections on $s$ are exact, taking $\mathrm H^0$ commutes with evaluation and gives $\mathrm H^0(\iota_{Ra_*M})=\Gamma(s,j^h_{a_*M})\circ\sigma_{a_*M}$, with no additional derived correction.

source.place: Step 2; explicit evaluation of the restriction--insertion--pullback point transport

proof.text: Evaluate the underived mate on the final object. The map $\sigma_{a_*M}$ first restricts a section along $(s\xrightarrow h s)\to(s\xrightarrow{\rm id}s)$ and inserts it into the inverse-image colimit. The colimit adjunction formula for pro-etale inverse image says that the counit in the transpose of $B_M$ is restriction along the corresponding Cartesian map. At the final object of $Y$, the composite of this map with the square identification $d_s$ is exactly $(Y\xrightarrow gY)\to(Y\xrightarrow{\rm id}Y)$. Therefore the resulting section is the restriction--insertion definition of $p_{g,M}$, and $\Gamma(s,B_M)\circ\sigma_{a_*M}=p_{g,M}$. This uses only final objects and the constant coefficient action, so it does not assume a $k$-linear Frobenius map.

source.place: Tags 00VE and 00WX, colimit adjunction formula for inverse image and its counit

proof.text: Finally, compose the first equality with the degree-zero point-transport equality. Because $(\lambda^h_{a_*M})^{-1}=j^h_{a_*M}$, exactness of sections gives $$\Gamma(Y,\lambda^g_M)\circ\mathrm H^0(\tau_M)=\Gamma(s,B_M)\circ\sigma_{a_*M}.$$ The preceding step identifies the right-hand side with $p_{g,M}$, proving the final formula. The calculation is unchanged for $M=0$, for $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and for disconnected $Y$ because every map was computed objectwise on the sites.
